description: AstroMetric combines full-stack software engineering, data science, and creative problem-solving to turn complex challenges into impactful solutions. We build intuitive experiences, effective data visualizations, and reliable systems that enable better decisions, improve traceability, eliminate operational blind spots, and automate processes. Driven by innovation, collaboration, and engineering best practices, we aim to explore new technologies and push beyond conventional solutions.
summary:
FLARE (Flame Analysis & Research Explorer) is an AI/SI-powered Decision Intelligence Platform that transforms decades of fragmented NASA combustion data into life-saving spacecraft fire safety protocols.
By integrating four rigorous analytical engines—a Thermodynamic Mission-Matcher, an Out-Of-Distribution Partial-Gravity ML Predictor for lunar and Martian environments, an Experimental Diff-Engine, and a Zero-Hallucination RAG Copilot with strict deterministic validation—FLARE instantly audits materials, predicts flammability gaps, and generates actionable safety reports. Beyond deep space exploration, FLARE’s aerosol data analysis drives terrestrial spinoffs, eliminating optical sensor false alarms in underground mining operations.
details:
FLARE (Flame Analysis & Research Explorer)

What does it do or how does it work? FLARE is a Decision Intelligence Platform that transforms over 30 years of fragmented NASA microgravity combustion data into actionable fire safety protocols for deep space exploration. Instead of a generic search tool, FLARE operates as a guided 3-step console driven by four independent analytical engines:

  1. Thermodynamic Mission-Matcher: Calculates a weighted Euclidean distance to instantly rank NASA PSI investigations against custom habitat parameters like Oxygen, Pressure, and Ventilation Flow.
  2. OOD Partial-Gravity Predictor: Uses Gaussian Process Regression (Matérn 3/2 kernel) in Log and Logit transformed latent spaces to predict flame spread and Minimum Oxygen Concentration (LOI). It bounds predictions for the Moon and Mars using 0g, 1g, and E-FIELD ion-wind analogs.
  3. Experimental Diff-Engine: Automatically isolates controlled versus iterated variables within a single experiment using normalized dispersion, and evaluates head-to-head similarities across studies using the Generalized Gower index.
  4. Zero-Hallucination Grounded Copilot (Hybrid RAG): A dual-retrieval system (Vector + TF-IDF) fortified by a deterministic Python double-barrier that strictly enforces verbatim quote extraction and automated numerical auditing.

What benefits does it have? FLARE drastically reduces the time aerospace engineers spend correlating experimental conditions. It automatically audits materials against the NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 baseline, instantly exposing "negative safety margins"—such as PMMA burning at 16.6% O2 under slow spacecraft ventilation (10cm/s), which is 1.0 point below the Earth-based safety threshold. Finally, it translates complex physics into a downloadable Decision Report mapped directly to NASA's pillars of Fire Prevention, Detection, and Suppression.

What is the intended impact of the project? For space exploration, FLARE prevents catastrophic fires in oxygen-enriched environments like the Artemis Moon Base (30% O2, 10.2 psi) by providing mathematically bounded predictions where no direct partial-gravity data currently exists. Terrestrially, FLARE delivers immediate industrial impact: by cross-referencing space-derived aerosol distributions from the SAME (smoke) and DAFT (dust) experiments, our platform isolates overlapping particle sizes to recalibrate optical sensors, eliminating false fire alarms in underground mining operations in Antofagasta, Chile.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Frontend & Architecture: Built with Next.js 15 (TypeScript), Tailwind CSS, Shadcn/ui, and Recharts for high-density, interactive data visualizations.
  • Backend & Data Science: Python powered by FastAPI. We utilized Scikit-Learn for Machine Learning (Gaussian Process and HistGradientBoosting regressors), SciPy, and NumPy for numerical quadrature and deterministic validations.
  • Database & AI: Deployed on Supabase (PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension) to handle relational metadata and semantic search. We integrated LLM APIs (Gemini 2.5 Flash / Groq Llama 3.3) restricted strictly to Structured JSON Outputs.
